translation.Coach.Lesson.anastasiaMate.Text: A knight on e7 takes g8 and g6 from the king in the corner, and its own pawn is in the way. Then one check on the h-file is enough. Give mate.
translation.Coach.Lesson.anastasiaMate.Title: Anastasia's mate
translation.Coach.Lesson.arabianMate.Text: Rook and knight work together: the rook checks right next to the king, the knight protects it and takes the last escape square. One of the oldest mating patterns of all. Give the Arabian mate.
translation.Coach.Lesson.arabianMate.Title: Arabian mate
translation.Coach.Lesson.backRank.Text: The king sits behind its own pawns without an escape square. A rook or queen on the back rank is mate right away. That's why players often push a pawn in front of the king. Here you deliver the mate.
translation.Coach.Lesson.backRank.Title: Back rank mate
translation.Coach.Lesson.bodenMate.Text: Two bishops cross their diagonals in front of the king. It is walled in by its own pieces: one bishop gives check, the other covers the escape squares. Mate with the bishop.
translation.Coach.Lesson.bodenMate.Title: Boden's mate
translation.Coach.Lesson.breakthrough.Text: Three pawns against three, and still one of them queens: a pawn sacrifice tears the chain open, and after the captures another pawn runs through. Find the breakthrough.
translation.Coach.Lesson.breakthrough.Title: Pawn breakthrough
translation.Coach.Lesson.castle.Text: A king in the center is an open target. Castling brings it behind its pawns and the rook into play. The squares in between must be empty and not attacked. Castle in each task.
translation.Coach.Lesson.castle.Title: King safety
translation.Coach.Lesson.decoy.Text: Sometimes you sacrifice a piece only to lure an enemy piece onto a certain square. There it is in the way or walks into a fork. Find the sacrifice that lures.
translation.Coach.Lesson.decoy.Title: Decoy
translation.Coach.Lesson.desperado.Text: If you have no other moves left, stalemate can save you. Your rook gives check after check. If it is taken, your king is stalemated and the game is a draw. Give check with the rook.
translation.Coach.Lesson.desperado.Title: Saved by stalemate
translation.Coach.Lesson.discovered.Text: A piece stands in front of its own long-range piece. When it moves away, the piece behind gives check. The front piece may attack freely, because your opponent must save the king first. Find the best discovery.
translation.Coach.Lesson.discovered.Title: Discovered check
translation.Coach.Lesson.doubleCheck.Text: Two pieces give check at the same time. Capturing or blocking does not help, the king has to move. Your moving piece may even take the queen. Give double check.
translation.Coach.Lesson.doubleCheck.Title: Double check
translation.Coach.Lesson.fork.Text: One piece attacks two at once, that's a fork. The knight is great at it because it jumps around corners. If it also gives check, your opponent must save the king and the other piece falls. Find the fork.
translation.Coach.Lesson.fork.Title: The fork
translation.Coach.Lesson.hanging.Text: A piece hangs when it is attacked and nobody defends it. Then you can simply take it. Before every move, look: what hangs for my opponent, and what hangs for me? Take the hanging piece in each task.
translation.Coach.Lesson.hanging.Title: Hanging pieces
translation.Coach.Lesson.mate.Text: Check means the king is attacked. Mate means it can no longer escape, and the game is over. Here queen and bishop play a duet on f7. Mate in one move in each task.
translation.Coach.Lesson.mate.Title: Check and mate
translation.Coach.Lesson.opposition.Text: When the kings face each other with one square between them, the side to move has to give way. Whoever has the opposition wins the pawn endgame. Put your king in front of your pawn and take the opposition.
translation.Coach.Lesson.opposition.Title: Opposition
translation.Coach.Lesson.overload.Text: A piece cannot guard two things at once. If it has to capture, it gives up its other job, often the back rank. Strike where the defender is overloaded.
translation.Coach.Lesson.overload.Title: Overloading
translation.Coach.Lesson.pin.Text: A piece is pinned when its king stands behind it. It may not move away then. Bishops, rooks and queens can pin. Pin a piece to its king in each task.
translation.Coach.Lesson.pin.Title: The pin
translation.Coach.Lesson.queenMate.Text: The queen can't do it alone, she needs her king as company. Drive the enemy king to the edge. Then the queen steps right in front of it, covered by her own king. Make sure it can still move, or it's stalemate.
translation.Coach.Lesson.queenMate.Title: Mate with the queen
translation.Coach.Lesson.removeDefender.Text: If only one piece guards the key square, simply take it. Then the defence collapses, here with mate on h7. Capture the defender.
translation.Coach.Lesson.removeDefender.Title: Removing the defender
translation.Coach.Lesson.rookMate.Text: With a rook it only works on the edge. Your king faces the other one and takes the squares in front of it. The rook then shuts the whole edge. Find the mating move each time.
translation.Coach.Lesson.rookMate.Title: Mate with the rook
translation.Coach.Lesson.skewer.Text: A skewer is a pin turned around: the more valuable piece stands in front. You give check, the king must move, and you take the piece behind it. Find the move that skewers king and piece.
translation.Coach.Lesson.skewer.Title: The skewer
translation.Coach.Lesson.smothered.Text: The king is walled in by its own pieces. A single knight is then enough to mate. It's the quietest final chord in chess. Mate with the knight.
translation.Coach.Lesson.smothered.Title: Smothered mate
translation.Coach.Lesson.square.Text: Draw a square from the passed pawn to its promotion rank. If your king is inside it or can step in, it catches the pawn. Step into the square with your king.
translation.Coach.Lesson.square.Title: The rule of the square
translation.Coach.Lesson.underpromotion.Text: A pawn does not always have to become a queen. A knight gives check where the queen cannot and forks king and queen. Promote to the right piece.
translation.Coach.Lesson.underpromotion.Title: Underpromotion
translation.Coach.Lesson.values.Text: Pawn 1, knight and bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9. When you can take several pieces, take the most valuable one. Here the bishop is worth more than the pawn. Pick the best catch in each task.
translation.Coach.Lesson.values.Title: Piece values

translation.Settings.Cloud.NotAllowed.Desc: The JBLBase cloud is private. Confirm your e-mail address first if you have not done so yet. Otherwise ask the operator to approve your account. Until then everything stays on this device.
translation.Settings.Cloud.NotVerified: Your e-mail address is not confirmed yet.
translation.Settings.Cloud.Registered: Account created. Please confirm your e-mail address with the link in the mail.
translation.Settings.Cloud.ResetSent: If an account exists for this e-mail, a reset mail is on its way.
translation.Settings.Cloud.RoleAdmin.Desc: Evaluations are stored without a depth limit, and you may write to the shared position store.
translation.Settings.Cloud.RoleUser.Desc: Evaluations are stored up to depth 28, mates always.
translation.Settings.Cloud.SignedOut.Desc: With an account, repertoires and training progress are synced between your devices. Without one the app works as before.
translation.Settings.Cloud.Sync.ConflictCopies: A repertoire was changed on two devices at once. The newer version counts; the other one was kept as a copy:
translation.Settings.Cloud.Sync.ConflictShort: Conflict: one version was kept as a copy
translation.Settings.Cloud.Sync.DeletionsHeld: Many repertoires are suddenly missing from this folder. To be safe, nothing was deleted in the cloud.
translation.Settings.Cloud.Sync.Desc: Repertoires and training progress are synced automatically: at start, within seconds of a change on another device, and shortly after changes on this one.
translation.Settings.Cloud.Sync.Limited: Daily limit reached: sync resumes tomorrow
translation.Settings.Cloud.Sync.Limited.Desc: Your account has synced unusually much with the cloud today, far more than normal use. To protect the cloud, syncing pauses until tomorrow. Your data on this device stays complete.
translation.Settings.Cloud.Sync.Offline: Offline: changes sync as soon as you are back online
translation.Settings.Cloud.Sync.TooBig: Too big for the cloud (over 900 KB even compressed), so not uploaded: {{files}}
translation.Settings.Cloud.Sync.Usage: Today on this device: {{reads}} read, {{writes}} written (position store {{evalReads}} / {{evalWrites}}). All devices together: {{accountReads}} read, {{accountWrites}} written.
translation.Settings.CoachCoordinates.Desc: Shows a-h and 1-8 on the board when you play against JBL
translation.Settings.ConsecutiveArrows.Desc: Show multiple arrows for the best line, if it involves moving the same piece several times
translation.Settings.DefaultPanelTab.Desc: The tab a game or analysis board opens on (repertoires open on Practice)
translation.Settings.Directories.Databases.Desc: This is where your databases are stored
translation.Settings.Directories.Desc: Customize the directories used by the app
translation.Settings.Directories.Engines.Desc: This is where your engine binaries and configuration are stored
translation.Settings.Directories.Files.Desc: This is where your games in the Files page are stored
translation.Settings.Directories.Puzzles.Desc: This is where your puzzle databases are stored
translation.Settings.EraseDrawablesOnClick.Desc: Clear the board of drawn arrows & circles by left-clicking the mouse
translation.Settings.EvalCache.ClearConfirm: Click again to delete all stored evaluations
translation.Settings.EvalCache.CloudCapped: Today's limit is reached so the cloud stays within the free quota. The rest follows tomorrow.
translation.Settings.EvalCache.CloudEnabledAdmin: As an admin your evaluations go, without a depth limit, to the shared store that every account reads.
translation.Settings.EvalCache.CloudEnabledUser: Your evaluations (up to depth 28, mates always) go to your cloud area and reach your other devices, so a position is only computed once.
translation.Settings.EvalCache.CloudMinDepthDesc: The engine recomputes shallower results faster than the sync takes.
translation.Settings.EvalCache.CloudSharedDesc: Also fetches the evaluations admins provide for everyone.
translation.Settings.EvalCache.CloudSignedOut: Sign in under Profile & accounts so your devices share their evaluations.
translation.Settings.EvalCache.CloudStatus: Last sync: {{uploaded}} uploaded, {{downloaded}} downloaded ({{applied}} taken over because deeper), {{pending}} still waiting.
translation.Settings.EvalCache.Desc: Every position an engine evaluates is stored locally and reused the next time you analyse it
translation.Settings.EvalCache.Session: Since the app started: {{lookups}} positions looked up, {{hits}} found in the cache, {{saved}} engine searches saved
translation.Settings.EvalCache.Unavailable: The position cache could not be opened
translation.Settings.FlipBoardAfterMove.Desc: Automatically flip the board after making a move on human games
translation.Settings.Inputs.SpellCheck.Desc: Enable or disable spell check on text inputs
translation.Settings.MaterialDisplay.Desc: Show net material difference or all captured pieces
translation.Settings.MoveHighlight.Desc: Show highlight for last move and check
translation.Settings.MoveMethod.Desc: Move pieces by dragging, clicking, or both
translation.Settings.MoveNotation.Desc: Choose how to display pieces in notation
translation.Settings.PieceAnimation.Desc: How fast pieces move on the board
translation.Settings.PieceDest.Desc: Show possible moves for each piece
translation.Settings.PreviewBoard.Desc: Show a preview of the board when hovering over a move in the engine analysis
translation.Settings.Privacy.Legal.Desc: JBLBase sends no usage data without your agreement. Here you find the privacy policy and the terms of use of the JBLBase account (in German).
translation.Settings.Privacy.UsageStats.Desc: Sends to Google Analytics which pages and features of the app are used, to show what is needed. No games, positions, names or account data. Off unless you switch it on.
translation.Settings.Repertoire.AdvanceDelay.Desc: How long the position stays after a correct move before the next one comes
translation.Settings.Repertoire.AutoDifficulty.Desc: A correct move under 30 seconds counts as Easy, slower as Good, right only on the second try as Hard, wrong twice as Again. After a correct move the next position follows without a click.
translation.Settings.Repertoire.Depth.Desc: Minimum number of games for a move to be considered relevant
translation.Settings.Repertoire.MainOwner.Desc: Your own repertoires are listed under this name. Use the same name as on your player card so they are compared with your games. It is only stored on this device. Without a name they are called "Ich".
translation.Settings.Repertoire.Trash.Desc: How long deleted repertoires are kept before they are removed for good
translation.Settings.ScrollThroughMoves.Desc: Enable or disable scrolling through moves on the chessboard
translation.Settings.Sound.Coach.Desc: JBL plays quiet sounds for good and bad moves and at the end of the game
translation.Settings.Tutorials.Desc: Step-by-step guides through the app. Start any of them again at any time.
translation.Settings.VariationArrows.Desc: Show thin grey arrows for the next move of every variation in the current position
translation.Tactics.MinMoves: At least this many own moves in the solution
translation.Tactics.MinMovesHint: 1 takes everything, from 2 on only combinations.
translation.Tactics.Strictness.Label: Strictness
translation.Tactics.Strictness.looseHint: More puzzles, including easy ones and some with a second usable move.
translation.Tactics.Strictness.normalHint: One clearly best move after a real mistake of the opponent. Simple recaptures and taking a hanging piece do not count. Every tactic is checked again 4 plies deeper.
translation.Tactics.Strictness.strictHint: Nearly as strict as Lichess with its puzzles: a clear jump in the evaluation, the second best move holds next to nothing, a one-mover needs a real motif (fork, pin, discovery, sacrifice, mate …). Checked again 6 plies deeper.
translation.Tutorial.Account.Corner.Body: In the top right an icon shows whether sync is running or succeeded. An arrow appears as soon as a new version is ready.
translation.Tutorial.Account.Corner.Title: Always in view
translation.Tutorial.Account.Desc: Sign in, link Lichess and Chess.com and sync between devices.
translation.Tutorial.Account.Profile.Body: With an account, repertoires and practice progress are the same on all your devices. Without one, everything works locally. Here you also link Lichess and Chess.com.
translation.Tutorial.Account.Profile.Title: Your account
translation.Tutorial.Account.Sync.Body: Sync runs by itself at start and shortly after each change. Here you see the last state and can sync right away.
translation.Tutorial.Account.Sync.Title: Sync
translation.Tutorial.Account.Title: Account and sync
translation.Tutorial.Admin.Desc: Accounts, devices and cloud usage at a glance (admins only).
translation.Tutorial.Admin.Links.Body: Links at the bottom lead straight to Analytics, Firestore usage and budget. Sync errors and engine crashes are under Events in Analytics.
translation.Tutorial.Admin.Links.Title: More details
translation.Tutorial.Admin.Overview.Body: Active accounts and devices, usage of the last 7 days against the free Firebase quota, and accounts that hit a limit today.
translation.Tutorial.Admin.Overview.Title: Overview
translation.Tutorial.Admin.Title: Admin overview
translation.Tutorial.Board.Add.Body: This button adds the line up to the current position to a repertoire; the tree button below it takes all side variations along. It works in every game and analysis.
translation.Tutorial.Board.Add.Title: Take lines in
translation.Tutorial.Board.Analysis.Body: Stockfish or Patricia calculate here. Every evaluation goes into the position store and is there right away next time. In the sub-tab Brilliant you search for “!!” moves from the current position.
translation.Tutorial.Board.Analysis.Title: Engine and brilliant moves
translation.Tutorial.Board.Database.Body: Shows what is played in this position on Lichess, by masters, in your games or in your repertoires.
translation.Tutorial.Board.Database.Title: Database
translation.Tutorial.Board.Desc: Your repertoire on the board: enter moves, hints while building, practice, engine and database.
translation.Tutorial.Board.Done.Body: The last tutorial shows how to load your own games and compare them with your repertoire.
translation.Tutorial.Board.Done.Title: Done
translation.Tutorial.Board.Open.Body: Open a repertoire on the board: click “Open”.
translation.Tutorial.Board.Open.Title: Open a repertoire
translation.Tutorial.Board.Practice.Body: In the tab Practice you train your repertoire line by line: the program plays the opponent, you find your moves. Mistakes come back on a review schedule.
translation.Tutorial.Board.Practice.Title: Practice
translation.Tutorial.Board.Repertoire.Body: Shows for every position what you play in your repertoires. While you build, hints appear here: common opponent moves without an answer and, where you have no move yet, what is played most on Lichess. A click plays the move.
translation.Tutorial.Board.Repertoire.Title: Tab Repertoire
translation.Tutorial.Board.Title: Work on the board
translation.Tutorial.CoachIntro.Card.Body: This card always shows your next task.
translation.Tutorial.CoachIntro.Card.Title: This is where I live
translation.Tutorial.CoachIntro.Desc: Where the coach lives and where to find help.
translation.Tutorial.CoachIntro.Help.Body: If you get stuck anywhere, the question mark has the matching guide.
translation.Tutorial.CoachIntro.Help.Title: Ask here
translation.Tutorial.CoachIntro.Title: Coach card and help
translation.Tutorial.Databases.Add.Body: “Add new” turns a PGN file into a fast database or downloads ready-made collections. Your Chess.com and Lichess games land here automatically via User.
translation.Tutorial.Databases.Add.Title: Add a database
translation.Tutorial.Databases.Board.Body: Mark a database as reference database and the Database tab at the board shows under “Local” what was played in its games.
translation.Tutorial.Databases.Board.Title: Use it at the board
translation.Tutorial.Databases.Desc: Import PGNs, search games and view them as an opening tree.
translation.Tutorial.Databases.Details.Body: On the right: “Explore”, “Open as tree” for the opening tree, more PGNs with “Add games”, “Export to PGN” and clean-up (duplicates, empty games).
translation.Tutorial.Databases.Details.Title: Explore and maintain
translation.Tutorial.Databases.List.Body: One click selects a database, a double click opens it with its games, players and tournaments.
translation.Tutorial.Databases.List.Title: Your databases
translation.Tutorial.Databases.Title: Databases
translation.Tutorial.Engines.Add.Body: Download one, pick a cloud engine or add a program on your computer under “Local”.
translation.Tutorial.Engines.Add.Title: Add an engine
translation.Tutorial.Engines.Cache.Body: Every evaluation goes into the position store. When a position comes up again, by any move order, the result is there at once. Details under Settings → Position store.
translation.Tutorial.Engines.Cache.Title: Nothing is calculated twice
translation.Tutorial.Engines.Desc: Set up Stockfish and Patricia, adjust threads, hash and lines.
translation.Tutorial.Engines.List.Body: All engines are listed here. Stockfish is the strongest, Patricia plays more aggressively and likes gambits and sacrifices.
translation.Tutorial.Engines.List.Title: Your engines
translation.Tutorial.Engines.Settings.Body: Select an engine to set threads, hash and the number of lines. More threads and hash calculate faster, as far as your computer allows.
translation.Tutorial.Engines.Settings.Title: Settings
translation.Tutorial.Engines.Title: Engines
translation.Tutorial.Files.Desc: Organise PGN files for games, repertoires and tournaments.
translation.Tutorial.Files.Filter.Body: Shows only repertoires, games, tournaments, puzzles or others.
translation.Tutorial.Files.Filter.Title: Filter by type
translation.Tutorial.Files.New.Body: Search at the top; next to it you create a new PGN file or a folder.
translation.Tutorial.Files.New.Title: New file or folder
translation.Tutorial.Files.Title: Files
translation.Tutorial.Files.Tree.Body: Drag files into folders to sort them. A click shows the file's games on the right, “Open” puts them on the board.
translation.Tutorial.Files.Tree.Title: Folders and files
translation.Tutorial.Games.Add.Body: Add your Chess.com or Lichess account. Signed in to Lichess, the app also shows Lichess numbers in the tree and in the gap check.
translation.Tutorial.Games.Add.Title: Add an account
translation.Tutorial.Games.Desc: Connect Chess.com and Lichess accounts, download your games and compare your openings with your repertoire.
translation.Tutorial.Games.Done.Body: Every area has a short tutorial: use the question mark in the top right or Settings → Tutorials.
translation.Tutorial.Games.Done.Title: Done
translation.Tutorial.Games.Download.Body: The download button on the account card loads your games into a local database. After that it only fetches new games.
translation.Tutorial.Games.Download.Title: Download your games
translation.Tutorial.Games.Openings.Body: The tab Openings of your player card shows your openings as White and Black. “Compare with my opening book” puts them next to your repertoire.
translation.Tutorial.Games.Openings.Title: Your openings
translation.Tutorial.Games.Title: Load your games
translation.Tutorial.Games.Welcome.Body: Once the app knows your games, it shows which openings you really play and where you leave your repertoire.
translation.Tutorial.Games.Welcome.Title: Your games
translation.Tutorial.Home.Cards.Body: Every new tab starts here: play an engine, open an analysis board, create a repertoire, play JBL or solve puzzles.
translation.Tutorial.Home.Cards.Title: What do you want to do?
translation.Tutorial.Home.Coach.Body: This is JBL, your coach. The next task always shows here. Click the figure or “Open coach” to see everything planned for today.
translation.Tutorial.Home.Coach.Title: JBL Coach
translation.Tutorial.Home.Desc: Play, analyse, import games and reopen recent files.
translation.Tutorial.Home.Import.Body: Paste a PGN here, pick a PGN file or a game link from Lichess or Chess.com. The game opens for analysis.
translation.Tutorial.Home.Import.Title: Import a game
translation.Tutorial.Home.Recent.Body: Your latest files in one click. For repertoires a badge shows how many positions are due for practice.
translation.Tutorial.Home.Recent.Title: Recently opened
translation.Tutorial.Home.Tabs.Body: “+” opens more tabs, for example a game next to your repertoire. Tabs can be moved and closed.
translation.Tutorial.Home.Tabs.Title: Several tabs
translation.Tutorial.Home.Title: New tab
translation.Tutorial.Insight.Calibration.Body: Missed tactics become puzzles. Here they get an estimated Elo, calibrated against real Lichess puzzles.
translation.Tutorial.Insight.Calibration.Title: Elo of your tactics
translation.Tutorial.Insight.Desc: Analyse all your games: accuracy, blunders, missed tactics.
translation.Tutorial.Insight.Player.Body: Pick one account or all. “Add player” also adds a player from one of your databases, for example a friend.
translation.Tutorial.Insight.Player.Title: Whose games?
translation.Tutorial.Insight.Run.Body: Choose engine, depth and games per run, then “Start analysis”. The newest games come first; stopping loses nothing.
translation.Tutorial.Insight.Run.Title: Start the analysis
translation.Tutorial.Insight.Stats.Body: Accuracy, blunders and missed tactics, by month, game phase, colour, time control and opening. A click on a move opens the game at that point.
translation.Tutorial.Insight.Stats.Title: Where you drop points
translation.Tutorial.Insight.Title: Insight
translation.Tutorial.Puzzles.Blind.Body: Look at the position for 10 to 30 seconds, then the pieces disappear and you solve from memory. Optionally with square names or typed moves.
translation.Tutorial.Puzzles.Blind.Title: Solve blind
translation.Tutorial.Puzzles.Database.Body: Pick a puzzle database. “Add new” downloads the Lichess puzzles or adds a file of your own.
translation.Tutorial.Puzzles.Database.Title: Choose puzzles
translation.Tutorial.Puzzles.Desc: Train tactics, puzzles from your own games, streak and blind mode.
translation.Tutorial.Puzzles.Mode.Body: Training picks puzzles from your rating range, optionally getting harder. In streak every solved puzzle is harder, until the first mistake.
translation.Tutorial.Puzzles.Mode.Title: Training or streak
translation.Tutorial.Puzzles.Open.Title: Open puzzles
translation.Tutorial.Puzzles.Own.Body: The target searches your own games with the engine for tactics you missed and turns them into puzzles. For a repertoire, use “Search tactics” on its card.
translation.Tutorial.Puzzles.Own.Title: From your games
translation.Tutorial.Puzzles.Stats.Body: The statistics show your puzzle Elo, accuracy and time. Next to them are reported puzzles and the settings.
translation.Tutorial.Puzzles.Stats.Title: Progress
translation.Tutorial.Puzzles.Title: Puzzles and tactics
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.Card.Body: Every repertoire has a card with its moves, lines and depth. The icons at the top right move it into a folder, show its import history or put it in the trash.
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.Card.Title: Your repertoire card
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.Check.Body: “Find gaps” tells you step by step what is missing next: opponent moves that come up often on Lichess but have no answer in your repertoire yet. Your own moves and move 1 are left out. The most important next step is always on top, and you can stop the search at any time.
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.Check.Title: Find gaps
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.Compare.Body: “Compare with my games” puts the games you played next to the repertoire. Click it.
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.Compare.Title: Compare with real games
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.CompareBack.Body: The arrow takes you back to the overview.
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.CompareBack.Title: Back
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.CompareLists.Body: Three lists show where you get surprised (an opponent move without an answer), where you deviate yourself and where your repertoire ends although your games go on. A click opens the line on the board, from there you add it to the repertoire.
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.CompareLists.Title: Where your games leave the repertoire
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.ComparePlayer.Body: Here you choose whose games count. You download your Chess.com and Lichess games under User (there is a tutorial for that, too).
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.ComparePlayer.Title: Whose games?
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.CompareTree.Body: Below, your games form a tree with the number of games and results. The border shows: green in the repertoire, orange a surprise, red a deviation, blue where the repertoire ends.
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.CompareTree.Title: Your games as a tree
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.Create.Body: One click creates your two main repertoires for White and Black. “New repertoire” adds more, e.g. one for a friend or one per opening: name, for whom, color and folder (subfolders with “/”, like “1.d4/London System”).
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.Create.Title: Create a repertoire
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.Desc: Create a repertoire, look at its opening tree, find gaps and compare it with your games.
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.Next.Body:
• Practice: open a repertoire → tab Practice → Lines.
• Your own games: User → add an account.
• Brilliant moves: “Search tactics” on the card, or the tab Brilliant on the analysis board.
• Engines: Stockfish and Patricia under Engines.
The next tutorial shows the work on the board.
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.Next.Title: What next?
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.Open.Body:
“Open” shows the repertoire on the board. Just play your moves and the opponent's answers; variations appear by themselves and everything is saved automatically.
From any other game or analysis you take a line in with the bookmark button below “Flip board”.
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.Open.Title: Enter your first moves
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.Title: Build a repertoire
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.Tree.Body: “Tree” shows your repertoire as a drawn tree. Click it now.
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.Tree.Title: Open the opening tree
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.TreeBack.Body: The arrow at the top left takes you back to your repertoires.
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.TreeBack.Title: Back to the overview
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.TreeDiagram.Body: The tree branches from left to right. Light boxes are White's moves, dark ones Black's, your own moves have a blue border. The blue bar shows how often a move is played on Lichess, the green one how many of your lines follow it. A dashed move is a common opponent move your repertoire does not have yet.
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.TreeDiagram.Title: Your variations
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.TreePreview.Body: Click a move to see the position on the small board, with arrows for your repertoire moves (green) and the main Lichess move (blue). You can move there too: once you leave the repertoire, “Add line” takes the new line in.
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.TreePreview.Title: Look at a position
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.Welcome.Body:
A repertoire holds the openings you want to play: your moves and your answers to the opponent's moves.
This tutorial shows in a few steps how to create one, look at it as a tree, find its gaps and compare it with your real games. You can start it again at any time under Settings → Tutorials.
translation.Tutorial.Repertoire.Welcome.Title: Welcome to your repertoires
translation.Tutorial.Settings.Desc: Settings, position store, bug reports and this help menu.
translation.Tutorial.Settings.EvalCache.Title: Position store
translation.Tutorial.Settings.EvalCachePanel.Body: How many positions are stored, per engine and depth, and how often the store has saved engine time. With an account your devices share their evaluations.
translation.Tutorial.Settings.EvalCachePanel.Title: Stored evaluations
translation.Tutorial.Settings.Help.Body: The question mark starts the tutorial for the page you are on.
translation.Tutorial.Settings.Help.Title: Help on every page
translation.Tutorial.Settings.Menu.Body: The gear in the top right jumps straight to any setting. It also has “Check for updates” and “Report a bug”, which copies version and log and opens a GitHub issue.
translation.Tutorial.Settings.Menu.Title: Quick menu
translation.Tutorial.Settings.Tabs.Body: On the left the sections: board, inputs, appearance, sound, shortcuts, folders, repertoire (with backups) and tutorials.
translation.Tutorial.Settings.Tabs.Title: All settings
translation.Tutorial.Settings.Title: Settings and help
translation.Tutorial.Share.Button.Body: The share icon on the card gives this one repertoire to another JBLBase account, by e-mail address or Lichess name. You need to be signed in.
translation.Tutorial.Share.Button.Title: Share
translation.Tutorial.Share.Desc: Give a repertoire to friends and pass on updates automatically.
translation.Tutorial.Share.Received.Body: What others share with you appears on this page to accept. You can view and practise shared repertoires, and edit them after “Create own copy”.
translation.Tutorial.Share.Received.Title: Shared with you
translation.Tutorial.Share.Title: Share a repertoire
translation.Tutorial.Share.Updates.Body: Once accepted, the other person gets each of your changes with the next sync. “Withdraw” stops the updates; their copy stays.
translation.Tutorial.Share.Updates.Title: Always up to date
translation.Updater.Available.Message: JBLBase {{version}} is available (installed: {{current}}). Install now? The app restarts afterwards.
translation.Updater.Available.Title: Update available
translation.UsageStats.Prompt.Text: With your agreement the app counts anonymously which pages and features are used and sends that to Google Analytics. No games, positions, names or account data. You can switch it off at any time under Settings → Privacy.
translation.UsageStats.Prompt.Title: Will you help to make JBLBase better?
